mainTopic: שבועות יט. — Knowing the exact cause of one's טומאה (רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא), forgetting both the טומאה and the מקדש, and the case of two doubtful paths.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about whether a person who entered the מקדש while טמא must know exactly what made him טמא. First it shows how רבי אליעזר uses the extra words in the פסוק in other ways: the list of animals is there for רבי's teaching, and 'בה' excludes a מתעסק. Then רבי יוחנן says the two תנאים agree in practice and argue only about which פסוק teaches the rule. רב ששת seems to agree, since he freely swapped their names. Next רבא asks רב נחמן about someone who forgot both that he was טמא and that he was in the מקדש. רב נחמן says he is חייב. רב אשי suggests watching which reminder makes him leave, but רבינא shows this test does not work, so there is no difference between the two ways of leaving, and רש״י explains that he is פטור. Finally a ברייתא brings a case of two paths, one טמא and one טהור, with רבי שמעון disagreeing. The גמרא begins to question the claim that רבי שמעון exempts 'in all of them', and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the verse lists שרץ according to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אליעזר, בהמה and חיה are written for רבי's teaching, and שרץ is simply written along with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah needs to write 'domesticated animal' and 'wild animal' for the teaching of רבי, it also writes 'creeping animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אליעזר deals with the list of חיה, בהמה and שרץ in the פסוק. רבי עקיבא used that list to prove that a person must know exactly what made him טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, the words בהמה and חיה are needed for a different lesson, which רבי taught earlier. Once the Torah is listing those, it also lists שרץ, even though שרץ teaches nothing new. So the list does not prove רבי עקיבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature whose carcass makes a person טמא
Like the teaching of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: Since it needs to write 'domesticated animal' and 'wild animal'
for the teaching of רבי,
phrases.notes: This is a teaching of רבי that the גמרא brought earlier, on דף ז.

phrases.english: it also writes 'creeping animal.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the passage by continuing the earlier defense of רבי אליעזר against the proof from the list of animals.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the extra words to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing each type of carcass separately seems to show that one must know exactly which one made him טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: בהמה and חיה are needed for רבי's teaching, and שרץ is written only to complete the list.

steps.title: Support: the Torah repeats a passage for one new detail
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that the Torah may repeat a whole passage just to add one new point.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: every passage that was said and then said again was repeated only for the new thing added in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known rule to show that it is normal for the Torah to write words that teach nothing new, as long as something else in the passage is new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports step 1. Writing שרץ again is not a problem, because the Torah often repeats material when it adds one new idea, here רבי's teaching. Extra words in a repeated passage are therefore not always a source for a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
A section or passage of the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule used across שס: a repeated Torah passage may exist just to add one new detail.

phrases.english: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Every passage that was stated and then repeated,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִשְׁנֵית אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ.
phrases.english: was repeated only for the new thing that was added in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 1 with a general rule about how the Torah writes.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah can write שרץ without it teaching anything new
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל about repeated passages

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from the word 'בה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר uses the word 'בה' ('in which he sinned').
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with this word 'בה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'בה' teaches according to רבי אליעזר. That word was used to show that a person must know exactly what sin he did, and רבי אליעזר does not accept that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר does not need 'בה' to require exact knowledge, the word seems extra for him. The גמרא wants to know what lesson he takes from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In it', from 'the sin in which he sinned'
What does he do with it? (How does he use this word?)

phrases.english: And רבי אליעזר,
what does he do with this word 'in it'?
phrases.notes: This is 'the sin in which he sinned,' the word used to teach that a person must know exactly what sin he did.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הַאי בָּהּ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the list of animals, the גמרא turns to the second source, the word 'בה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from the word 'בה'

steps.title: 'בה' excludes a מתעסק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses 'בה' to exclude a person who acted without intending the act at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude a מתעסק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי אליעזר, 'בה' teaches that a מתעסק, someone busy with something else who did the act without meaning to, does not bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the word is not extra for רבי אליעזר. It sets a different limit: liability applies only when a person meant to do the act, even if he did not know it was forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who does an act without meaning to do it, while busy with something else

steps.confusionAlert: A מתעסק is not the same as a שוגג. A שוגג meant to do the act but did not know it was forbidden. A מתעסק did not mean to do the act at all.

phrases.english: To exclude one who acts unawares.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר uses 'בה' to exclude a מתעסק from bringing a קרבן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they disagree only about the source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא agree on the law and disagree only about which פסוק teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is only in how they explain the verses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different view from חזקיה's. He says the two תנאים have no practical disagreement at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חזקיה, רבי עקיבא requires exact knowledge of the טומאה and רבי אליעזר does not. רבי יוחנן says both agree that one must know the exact source of his טומאה. They argue only about how to read the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: How the verses are explained; which verse teaches the law

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the picture of the whole מחלוקת. It is not a disagreement about practical law, only about the source.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:
The difference between them is only in how they explain the verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מַשְׁמָעוּת דּוֹרְשִׁין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to חזקיה's explanation, which the earlier steps were following.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא agree in practice and differ only in how they read the פסוקים.

steps.title: רב ששת agrees, since he swaps the two names
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת also seems to hold that there is no practical difference, because he freely switches the names of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רב ששת: the difference between them is only in how they explain the verses. For רב ששת would switch the opinion of רבי אליעזר to רבי עקיבא and the opinion of רבי עקיבא to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב ששת holds like רבי יוחנן. The proof is that he did not care which opinion he gave to which תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two views led to different practical results, it would matter who said what. Since רב ששת swapped the names freely, he must have held that they differ only about the source.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to understand the מחלוקת. חזקיה says there is a practical difference about knowing the exact טומאה. רבי יוחנן, and apparently רב ששת, say it is only about which פסוק teaches the rule.

phrases.english: And so said רב ששת:
The difference between them is only in how they explain the verses.
For רב ששת would switch
the opinion of רבי אליעזר to רבי עקיבא
and the opinion of רבי עקיבא to רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's view by showing that רב ששת held the same way.
steps.raayaObject: That רב ששת agrees there is no practical difference
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ששת's habit of swapping the two opinions

steps.title: רבא asks about forgetting both the טומאה and the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the law is when a person forgot both that he was טמא and that he was in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: if he forgot both this and that, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא asks about someone who forgot that he was טמא and also forgot that he was in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of forgetting has its own law, so the question is which one decides the case. When both happen together, it is unclear whether he brings a קרבן.

phrases.english: רבא asked רב נחמן:
If he had a lapse of awareness of both this and that, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means he forgot both that he was טמא and that he was in the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, separate from the רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether someone who forgot both the טומאה and the מקדש brings a קרבן

steps.title: רב נחמן: he forgot the טומאה, so he is חייב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that since he forgot his טומאה, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: he has a lapse of awareness about his טומאה, and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules that the person is חייב, because forgetting the טומאה is part of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forgetting the טומאה is enough to make a person חייב. רב נחמן holds that adding a second kind of forgetting does not take that away.

phrases.english: He said to him:
He has a lapse of awareness about his impurity, and he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הֲרֵי הֶעְלֵם טוּמְאָה בְּיָדוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is חייב, because he forgot his טומאה.

steps.title: On the contrary: he forgot the מקדש, so he should be פטור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: you could just as well say he forgot the מקדש, so he should be פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: he has a lapse of awareness about the מקדש, and he should be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's answer by looking at the other kind of forgetting in the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forgetting the מקדש on its own makes a person פטור. Since that is also part of this case, the גמרא asks why the טומאה side should decide it. The same facts can be argued in the opposite direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgetting that one is in the מקדש

phrases.english: On the contrary:
He has a lapse of awareness about the Temple, and he should be exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the person is חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case also includes forgetting the מקדש, which leads to פטור. So there is no reason the טומאה side should decide the case over the מקדש side.

steps.title: רב אשי: Watch what makes him leave
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the problem from step 9. We can tell which forgetting was the real one by watching which reminder makes the person leave the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We watch him. If he leaves because he is told he is טמא, then his forgetting was about the טומאה, and he is חייב. If he leaves because he is told he is in the מקדש, then his forgetting was about the מקדש, and he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a practical way to settle the problem raised in step 9. Look at what reminder actually gets the person to leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא said you could call it forgetting the מקדש just as easily as forgetting the טומאה. רב אשי says his behavior shows us which one he really forgot. If reminding him of his טומאה makes him leave, he had forgotten the טומאה, which makes him חייב. If reminding him of the מקדש makes him leave, he had forgotten the מקדש, which makes him פטור.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We observe.
If he leaves because of the impurity,
then he has a lapse of awareness of impurity, and he is liable.
If he leaves because of the Temple,
then he has a lapse of awareness of the Temple, and he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by offering a test that tells which forgetting was the real one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical test: his behavior shows which lapse he had
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There seemed to be no way to decide whether to treat the case as forgetting טומאה or forgetting מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Watch which reminder makes him leave, and rule according to that lapse.

steps.title: רבינא: Each reminder only works with the other
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי's test. Leaving the מקדש only happens because he also knows he is טמא, and leaving because of טומאה only happens because he also knows he is in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Does he leave the מקדש for any reason other than his טומאה? And does he leave because of his טומאה for any reason other than that he is in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רב אשי's test. Whichever reminder he hears, he leaves only because he now knows both facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being in the מקדש is no reason to leave unless you are טמא. Being טמא is no reason to leave unless you are in the מקדש. So the moment he walks out, he is aware of both facts, and his behavior cannot show which one was the real forgetting.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it anything (but...)? A word that sets up 'only because'

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Did he leave because of the Temple
for any reason other than the impurity?
Did he leave because of the impurity
for any reason other than the Temple?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: כְּלוּם פֵּרֵישׁ מִמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's test from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's test of watching which reminder makes him leave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each reason to leave depends on the other fact, so leaving always reflects awareness of both and cannot show which lapse was the real one.

steps.title: There is no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבינא concludes that the two kinds of leaving are the same, so רב אשי's test does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: This closes רבינא's objection. The test fails because both ways of leaving come down to the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since leaving always happens with awareness of both טומאה and מקדש, his behavior cannot tell the two cases apart, so רב אשי's test is set aside. 'There is no difference' means the case is treated the same way no matter how he leaves. רש״י explains the result: he is פטור. Forgetting the מקדש is always part of the case too, and רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא exempt someone who forgot the מקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: When someone forgot both his טומאה and the מקדש, watching how he leaves cannot tell us which forgetting counts, because either reminder only works together with the other. רש״י says the upshot is that he is פטור, since forgetting the מקדש is always part of the case too.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבינא's challenge with its bottom line.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's test does not work, because there is no real difference between the two ways of leaving. Per רש״י, he is פטור either way, because he also forgot the מקדש.

steps.title: Two paths: walked the first without entering, then the second and entered
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: there are two paths, one טמא and one טהור. Someone walked the first and did not enter the מקדש, then walked the second and entered. He is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There are two paths, one טמא and one טהור. If someone walked on the first and did not enter the מקדש, then walked on the second and entered, he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about a person who is not sure which path made him טמא. In this first case he walks both paths before entering the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which path is the טמא one. Once he has walked on both, he has certainly passed over the טמא one. So when he enters the מקדש, he is definitely טמא, and he is חייב a קרבן.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי שְׁבִילִין, אֶחָד טָמֵא וְאֶחָד טָהוֹר;
phrases.english: Two paths, one impure and one pure;
phrases.notes: The ברייתא assumes we don't know which of the two paths is the טמא one.

phrases.english: and he walked on the first and did not enter,
then on the second and entered: he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic connected to awareness of טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After walking both doubtful paths, entering the מקדש makes him חייב, since he is certainly טמא.

steps.title: Entered after each path, with purification in between
steps.stepSummary: Second case of the ברייתא: he walked the first path and entered, purified himself fully, then walked the second path and entered. The ruling is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he walked on the first path and entered, then was sprinkled, sprinkled again, and immersed, and afterward walked on the second path and entered, he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a harder case. He enters the מקדש after each path, and he becomes טהור in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each entry alone is doubtful. The first path may have been the טהור one, and after the purification the second path may also have been the טהור one. Still, one of his two entries was certainly while he was טמא, and this opinion holds him חייב for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sprinkled (with the water that purifies from טומאת מת)

phrases.english: If he walked on the first and entered,
was sprinkled, sprinkled again, and immersed,
phrases.notes: These are the steps that purify someone from טומאת מת: sprinkling on the third and seventh days, then the מקוה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָלַךְ בַּשֵּׁנִי וְנִכְנַס – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and afterward walked on the second and entered: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ בָּרִאשׁוֹן וְנִכְנַס, הִזָּה וְשָׁנָה וְטָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same ברייתא, where each entry is doubtful on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion holds him חייב, since one of the two entries was certainly while טמא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון and רבי שמעון בן יהודה exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון exempts in the second case. רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting רבי שמעון, exempts in all the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון exempts him. And רבי שמעון בן יהודה exempts him in all of the cases in the name of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings opinions that disagree with the חייב ruling. Two versions of רבי שמעון's view are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון exempts in the second case, because neither single entry was certainly while טמא. רבי שמעון בן יהודה reports that רבי שמעון exempted in all the cases, which would include even the first case.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of them (all the cases)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר בְּכוּלָּן
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda exempts in all of them,
in the name of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinions to the rulings in steps 13 and 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון exempts in the second case. רבי שמעון בן יהודה, quoting him, exempts in all cases.

steps.title: Questioning 'in all of them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks up the words 'in all of them' to question them. The rest of the challenge comes next.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the words 'in all of them' and is about to ask how רבי שמעון בן יהודה could exempt in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All of them' seems to include the first case, where he walked both paths before entering and was certainly טמא. That looks hard to exempt, so the גמרא is preparing to challenge these words.

phrases.english: In all of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the end of step 15 to begin questioning it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'exempts in all of them' in רבי שמעון בן יהודה's report
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'All of them' would include the first case, where he was certainly טמא when he entered, and exempting there seems hard to explain.
